issues.title: [26.3 NeoForge] Startup crash: NPE in ScreenUtils.getScreen() when the early loading window was resized
issues.body:
**FancyMenu:** 3.9.14 (`fancymenu_neoforge_3.9.14_MC_26.3.jar`), Konkrete 1.11.1, Melody 1.0.17
**Loader:** NeoForge 26.3.0.83 (FML 12.0.12), early loading window enabled (default)

The game crashes on startup, before the title screen. It also happens with FancyMenu and its dependencies as the only mods in a clean profile.

```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "net.minecraft.client.gui.Gui.screen()" because "net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.getInstance().gui" is null
	at de.keksuccino.fancymenu.util.ScreenUtils.getScreen(ScreenUtils.java:29)
	at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.handler$bpj000$fancymenu$beforeResizeCurrentScreenFancyMenu(Minecraft.java)
	at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.resizeGui(Minecraft.java:1457)
	at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.framebufferSizeChanged(Minecraft.java:1451)
	at com.mojang.blaze3d.platform.Window.onFramebufferResize(Window.java:366)
	at net.neoforged.neoforge.client.loading.earlydisplay.EarlyWindowHandoff.completeWindowHandoff(EarlyWindowHandoff.java:61)
	at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.<init>(Minecraft.java:553)
	at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(Main.java:280)
```
Window dimensions in the crash report: old 854x480, new 1014x559.

**Cause:** NeoForge hands the early loading window over inside the `Minecraft` constructor. If the window size changed while the loading screen was shown, `completeWindowHandoff` calls `Window.onFramebufferResize` → `Minecraft.resizeGui()` before `Minecraft.gui` is assigned. FancyMenu's `beforeResizeCurrentScreenFancyMenu` handler calls `ScreenUtils.getScreen()`, which does `Minecraft.getInstance().gui.screen()`. On 26.3 the current screen lives in `Gui`, so this throws a NPE. The handler itself already checks the screen for `null`, so only `getScreen()` needs a guard.

**Suggested fix:**
```java
public static Screen getScreen() {
    Gui gui = Minecraft.getInstance().gui;
    return gui == null ? null : gui.screen();
}
```
We confirmed this guard works by injecting it at the head of `ScreenUtils.getScreen()` from our own mod.

issues.title: Allow WaterMedia 2.x to coexist when FancyMenu video features are unused
issues.body:
### Detailed Feature Description

## Use case

On Minecraft 1.21.1 / NeoForge 21.1.243, our pack uses FancyMenu 3.9.12 for a custom main menu (no FancyMenu video elements) and WaterFrames 2.1.23 for in-world TVs. WaterFrames 2.1.23 declares a required WaterMedia range of `[2.1.34,2.2)`, so we use WaterMedia 2.1.37. FancyMenu rejects it during mod loading, before we can reach the menu:

```
Mod fancymenu only supports watermedia 3.0.0.22 or above
Currently, watermedia is 2.1.37
```

Updating WaterMedia alone would violate WaterFrames' declared dependency. The WaterFrames author has confirmed that WaterFrames v3 with WaterMedia v3 support is in development: https://github.com/SrRapero720/WATERFRAMES/issues/300

## Request

Could FancyMenu provide a supported way to opt out of its WaterMedia integration when its video features are not used, so WaterMedia 2.x can coexist for another mod? Alternatively, could FancyMenu avoid rejecting WaterMedia 2.x at load time and disable only its own incompatible video features? If neither is technically safe because of class loading or API differences, a clarification would help modpack maintainers choose a path.

This is a compatibility request, not a request for FancyMenu to support video playback through WaterMedia 2.x. I can provide the archived mod-loading report if useful.

issues.title: Tree leaves disappear at a distance with FancyMenu 3.9.12 (fixed by F3+T, not present in 3.9.11)
issues.body: ### Detailed Bug Description ## Description After updating FancyMenu from 3.9.11 to 3.9.12, tree leaves become invisible at a distance, while the trunks remain visible. When approaching a tree, the leaves become visible again. However, they can disappear again while sprinting and reappear when standing still. Pressing F3+T (resource reload) immediately fixes the issue without changing any graphics settings. The trees remain normal when leaving and re-entering the world, but the issue returns after restarting Minecraft. Changing the mipmap level from 4 to 0 also fixes the issue, but changing it back to 4 does not bring the issue back until the game is restarted. F3+A (chunk reload) does not fix the issue. ## Troubleshooting performed * Disabled Sodium, Entity Culling, ImmediatelyFast, Dynamic FPS and FerriteCore, including testing with all five disabled simultaneously. The issue persisted. * Disabled the custom resource pack. The issue persisted. * Renamed the FancyMenu configuration directory to generate fresh default settings. The issue persisted. * Disabled FancyMenu entirely. The issue disappeared. * Re-enabled Just Zoom and Xaero's Minimap/World Map while keeping FancyMenu disabled. The issue did not return. * Downgraded FancyMenu to 3.9.11 and restored the original configuration. Everything worked normally. * Updated FancyMenu to 3.9.12 again. The issue immediately returned. * Tested vanilla Minecraft and a clean NeoForge installation without additional mods. Neither showed the issue. ## Environment * Minecraft: 26.1.2 * NeoForge: 26.1.2.109 * FancyMenu: 3.9.12 (affected), 3.9.11 (working) * GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 * Graphics driver: NVIDIA 616.92 * Operating system: Windows ## Expected behavior Tree leaves should render correctly immediately after launching the game, without requiring a manual resource reload. ## Additional information This appears to be a regression introduced in FancyMenu 3.9.12, or an interaction introduced by that version. I can provide screenshots, game logs, and additional mod configuration details if needed. ### How To Reproduce The Bug ## Steps to reproduce 1. Launch Minecraft 26.1.2 with NeoForge 26.1.2.109 and FancyMenu 3.9.12. 2. Enter a single-player world with mipmap level 4. 3. Look at trees in the distance. Their leaves are invisible, but their trunks are visible. 4. Press F3+T. The leaves immediately become visible. 5. Restart Minecraft. issues.title: Layout Auto-Saving & Backup System (History)
issues.body:
## Auto-Saving

- Existing layouts that are already saved as file should get auto-saved by the layout editor every **5 minutes**. There should be some sort of scheduler running with the layout editor for that.

## History Logic

- There should be a history system that keeps backups of all layout files.
- Backups get written while working on the layout, to save them only when the file is actually actively getting changed.
- The system saves backups every 10 minutes, and it can hold up to 50 layout snapshots/backups per layout file.
- When saving a backup, it should compare the last saved backup with the new one, to see if they are identical. When they are identical, do not save a new backup. Is-identical check should happen via the file directly, so maybe comparing the file text content or hash or something.
- It should also keep backups of layouts that get deleted, to be able to restore a deleted layout.
- The system should create a special backup snapshot right before deleting a layout, even if it gets deleted while the user is not in the layout editor.
- Whenever possible, it should save a low-res/compressed screenshot of the editor when creating a backup, so it can later be shown as tiny preview when managing/browsing backups in the UI, to see how the layout looked at the time of creating the backup.
- The history system should save all its stuff, including backups, to FancyMenu's instance data directory, NOT in the instance's `/config` folder. Should be in `FancyMenu.INSTANCE_DATA_DIR`.

## History UI

- The backup system should have a UI to browse backups for all layouts.
- The UI should let the user browse/restore/manage backups for all layouts that have backups saved, when the UI is not targeting a specific layout.
- In the layout editor there should be a "Restore from History" entry in the menu of the Edit tab of the menu bar, that opens the backup UI, but it should limit it to the specific layout that is open in the editor (it should "target" that specific layout).
- Outside the editor there should be a "Browse Layout History" entry in the layouts menu in the context menu where the user creates new layouts, that also opens the history browser, but without targeting a specific layout.
- In that same context menu outside the editor, there should also be an entry "Show History" in each layout's sub context menu (where it is possible to edit/toggle/delete a specific layout), and that entry should open the history browser targeting the specific layout it got opened from.
- The history/backup browser should make it possible to restore and delete specific backups/snapshots.
- It should also make it possible to clear the full history for a specific layout at once.
- And it should be possible to clear the WHOLE history of ALL layouts at once, basically purging the each layout's full history at once.
- It should show useful information for each backup in the history browser, like when a backup got saved, maybe how many elements are saved in it, file size, and so on.
- The history browser should be a popup window like most other UIs of FancyMenu.
- There should be entries in the Settings context menu of FancyMenu to disable auto-saving, and disable the layout history. Both should be Enabled/Disabled toggles.
- There should be a hotkey in the layout editor for quickly toggling auto-saving on/off by pressing a keyboard key combination. When toggling auto-saving with the hotkey, a toast notification (using MC's toast system) will show up, telling the user that auto-saving got enabled/disabled. The word "enabled" should show in light-green, and "disabled" in red. Toast should have no title/headline, just body text.
- When the editor auto-saved a layout, it should show a light-green message "Layout saved." where normally the "unsaved changes" message would be in the editor. The auto-save message show for 2 seconds after auto-saving.

issues.title: Add Scoreboard Placeholder Usage
issues.body:
### Detailed Feature Description

I suggest to add one type of scoreboard placeholder to work properly — reading a specified scoreboard score from an entity and returning that value.

One important detail is that the entity should not be limited to players — it should be any entity in the game that can be selected by a target selector (@e). But since reading a scoreboard is a one-to-one operation, the selected entity should be restricted in count, e.g., requiring at least an @e[limit=1] filter to ensure the process works correctly.

For example, a placeholder like:
{"placeholder":"scoreboard_score","values":{"entity":"@e[limit=1,sort=nearest,type=zombie]","objective":"Level"}}
— if the nearest zombie's 'Level' score is 5, the placeholder would return 5.

Another detail: if no matching entity can be found, perhaps the placeholder could return 0 as a fallback. For instance, if there are no zombies in the world, the placeholder would return 0. The target selector should support @s in addition to @e (support for @p and @r would also be beneficial, though less critical).

issues.title: Slider not working correctly when rotating it to slide vertically instead of horizontally

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body:
The slider is designed to slide only horizontally, not vertically; if the rotate function is used to rotate it by 90 degrees, the slider will glitch and not work correctly, because it still calculates sliding based on horizontal movement.

Should get fixed for custom Slider elements, and for Vanilla sliders. Probably best to fix that via Mixin.

The slide logic should always dynamically adjust to the rotation of the element, similar to how we handle the click hitbox of widgets/buttons when they are rotated.

issues.title: Add FancyMenu placeholder support to the Custom Window Title
issues.body:
### Detailed Feature Description

The **Custom Window Title** setting under:

`Customization -> Global Customizations -> Custom Window Title`

currently displays FancyMenu placeholders as literal text instead of resolving them.

For example, this:

```text
My Modpack v{"placeholder":"getvariable","values":{"name":"modpack_version"}}
```

is not resolved when used as the Minecraft window title.

It would be useful if the Custom Window Title supported the same FancyMenu placeholders as other compatible text fields, including:

- `getvariable`
- `modversion`
- `mcversion`
- Other supported placeholders

This would allow modpacks to display dynamic information, such as their current version, Minecraft version, or player name, in the Minecraft window title.

Ideally, the title should also update when a referenced variable changes.

**Expected result:**

```text
My Modpack v1.2.3
```

instead of displaying the placeholder syntax itself.

issues.title: Crash when adding a Player Entity Element in the layout editor
issues.body:
### Detailed Bug Description

I'm from China, and this text was translated and checked with the help of DeepSeek, which also helped analyze the crash cause.

Root cause observed:
The crash occurs because Forgery's mixin `use_player_list_name_in_tag` (in `Player.getDisplayName()`) tries to call `ClientPacketListener.getPlayerInfo(UUID)` to fetch the display name. However, in the main menu / layout editor, there is no active network connection – `Minecraft.getConnection()` returns `null` – causing a NullPointerException.

When FancyMenu renders a dummy player entity (`FancyPlayerMock`) in the layout editor, it calls `Player.getDisplayName()`, which triggers the Forgery mixin and leads to the crash.

I have also submitted the same crash report to Forgery's issue tracker, so both sides are aware of this compatibility issue.

Crash report is attached.

### How To Reproduce The Bug

1. Install FancyMenu (v3.9.9) and Forgery / Fabrication (v3.6.6+1.20) together in Minecraft 1.20.1 Forge.
2. Launch the game and open FancyMenu's layout editor.
3. Add a "Player Entity Element" to the layout.
4. The game crashes immediately with a NullPointerException (see attached crash report).

### Detailed Bug Description

I'm from China, and this text was translated and checked with the help of DeepSeek, which also helped analyze the crash cause.

Root cause observed:
The crash occurs because Forgery's mixin `use_player_list_name_in_tag` (in `Player.getDisplayName()`) tries to call `ClientPacketListener.getPlayerInfo(UUID)` to fetch the display name. However, in the main menu / layout editor, there is no active network connection – `Minecraft.getConnection()` returns `null` – causing a NullPointerException.

When FancyMenu renders a dummy player entity (`FancyPlayerMock`) in the layout editor, it calls `Player.getDisplayName()`, which triggers the Forgery mixin and leads to the crash.

I have also submitted the same crash report to Forgery's issue tracker, so both sides are aware of this compatibility issue.

Crash report is attached.

### How To Reproduce The Bug

1. Install FancyMenu (v3.9.9) and Forgery / Fabrication (v3.6.6+1.20) together in Minecraft 1.20.1 Forge.
2. Launch the game and open FancyMenu's layout editor.
3. Add a "Player Entity Element" to the layout.
4. The game crashes immediately with a NullPointerException (see attached crash report).

issues.title: Browser element: JS bridge actions fail with only-works-on-the-game-thread error since Rinku switch

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Since FancyMenu 3.9.x switched the browser engine from MCEF to Rinku, actions executed from the JavaScript bridge inside a **Browser element** fail with the "asynchronously execute" error dialog. The JS API is correct (`fancymenu.actions.execute` / `executeWithCallback`) and worked fine before with the MCEF/Konkrete bridge.

The new Rinku `ActionBridge` runs `ActionInstance.execute()` directly on the CEF browser thread. `Action.checkAsync()` then blocks every action with `canRunAsync() == false` because the current thread is not the game thread, and shows the error dialog.

**To Reproduce**

1. Minecraft 1.20.1 Forge, FancyMenu 3.9.9, Rinku 3.0.1
2. Add a Browser element to the title screen layout, loading a local HTML file (`config/fancymenu/assets/*.html`)
3. In the HTML:
```javascript
fancymenu.actions.executeWithCallback(
    'mimicbutton',
    'title_screen:mc_titlescreen_singleplayer_button',
    function() { console.log('ok'); },
    function(e) { console.error(e); }
);
```
4. Click the button -> error dialog:

```
Failed to execute FancyMenu action!
You tried to asynchronously execute an action that only works on the game thread.
The action is probably part of a Ticker element that runs in Async mode.

Action Name: Mimic Vanilla/Mod Button
```

**Expected behavior**

Actions execute on the game thread (as they did with the old MCEF/Konkrete bridge), so sync-only actions like `mimicbutton`, `opengui`, `back_to_last_screen`, `sendmessage` and `join_last_world_or_server` work from the browser.

**Root cause analysis (bytecode of FancyMenu 3.9.9)**

- `ActionBridge.handleActionRequest` -> `processAction` -> `executeAction(ActionInstance)` calls `ActionInstance.execute()` directly on the CEF message-router thread, with no dispatch to the game thread.
- `ActionInstance.execute()` calls `Action.checkAsync()` first; `checkAsync()` returns `false` when `!Minecraft.getInstance().isOnGameThread() && !canRunAsync()`, shows the `fancymenu.actions.async.cant_run_async` dialog, and the action never runs.
- Sync-only actions (`canRunAsync() == false`, verified via `javap`): `MimicButtonAction`, `OpenScreenAction`, `BackToLastScreenAction`, `SendMessageAction`, `JoinLastWorldServerAction`.
- Actions that do not override `canRunAsync()` (e.g. `QuitGameAction`, `ShowToastAction`) inherit `true` and work fine from the bridge.

**Suggestion**

Dispatch the action to the game thread inside the Rinku `ActionBridge` before calling `ActionInstance.execute()` (e.g. via `MainThreadTaskExecutor` or `Minecraft.getInstance().execute(...)`), matching the behavior of the old MCEF bridge.

**Basic Information**

- Minecraft version: 1.20.1
- Mod Loader: Forge 47.4.x (Java 17)
- FancyMenu version: 3.9.9
- Rinku 3.0.1, Konkrete 1.8.0, Melody 1.0.3
- Latest log: the error only appears as an in-game dialog, not in `latest.log`

### Detailed Feature Description

Currently the two ways I know of accepting a players input for a variable for something like note keeping or such where it is easy for the player to see what they are inputting is 1)Making a html that hooks into fancy menus but to make it seamless is not easy but is possible 2) In newer versions you can create a dialog via a command to allow the player to store the input into a variable. issues.title: Add back support for using Minecraft formatting codes (`§`/`&`) in "Text" elements

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body:
- Using Minecraft's normal automatic text formatting system isn't working well in Text elements, because they use a Markdown renderer under the hood, so we should simply add all normal Vanilla Minecraft formatting codes to the Markdown renderer's formatting code parser, so the Markdown renderer applies the formattings manually, instead of letting Minecraft do it.
- The normal automatic formatting isn't working good here, because Markdown renders text bodies in small chunks instead of one big string, which breaks the Vanilla formatting logic.
- Unlike normal Markdown, we should also include Minecraft's underline formatting code here.
- We need to make sure that the `§r`/`&r` code only affects other Vanilla Minecraft codes, and does not reset any other formatting logic.

issues.title: Villager Raid Information/Observation
issues.body:
It should be possible to get information about active raids. The "active" raid for the client is the one that the user sees displayed at the top of the screen (if any is displayed, otherwise the client should not see an active raid).

There should be the following ways to get information about raids:

- "Total Active Raid Waves" placeholder
- "Remaining Active Raid Waves" placeholder
- "Current Active Raid Wave" placeholder
- "Active Raid Alive Raiders Count" placeholder
- "Active Raid Alive Raiders List" placeholder (returns list of all raider entities (humanoid and non-humanoid ones) and separates them by comma without spaces; every list entry is built like `mob.identifier#entity_uuid`)
- Listener that triggers when a raid starts and the player is in the raid area while it starts
- Listener that triggers when entering an active raid area (should trigger only when entering the area of an already active raid, not when a raid starts)
- Listener that triggers when leaving an active raid area (same rules as listener above)
- Listener that triggers when a raid finishes while the player is in the raid area (provides custom variable that says if the raid ended in a victory or defeat)
- "Is In Active Raid Area" requirement

issues.title: Add a judgment to determine whether an entity matching the selector conditions can be selected.
issues.body:
### Detailed Feature Description

Add a return value that checks whether the written target selector can actually select the corresponding entity, returning `true` if it can.  
For example:  
- If the player itself has `tag=A` and `scoreboard={A=1}`, then using `@s[tag=A,scoreboard={A=1}]` would return `true`.  
- If there exists a zombie with `tag=A` and `scoreboard={A=1}`, then using `@e[tag=A,scoreboard={A=1},limit=1,type=minecraft:zombie]` would return `true`.  

Based on this functionality, it could also be extended to return the number of entities that match the selector — for example, if there are two zombies meeting the conditions, it would return `2`.



Based on what I know so far, the only way to use target selectors is through server-side NBT checking. Although that can indirectly verify whether a selector selects an entity, it's not very intuitive and requires binding an NBT retrieval function — and NBT retrieval itself comes with a huge performance cost. So I suggest adding the above functionality to avoid the performance overhead caused by NBT checks.

issues.title: [NF 1.21.1] Invisible screens when menu blur is enabled
issues.body:
### Detailed Bug Description

When running FancyMenu alongside certain mods while Minecraft's menu blur is enabled (for any value), screens from those mods will appear as invisible when rendered. This has probably been most commonly observed with Iris Shaders, but I've also discovered it more recently happening with the 1.21.1 version of Tensura: Reincarnated.

This issue appears identical to issue #1509, and there have since been folks who find that disabling blur is the easiest way to address the issue. But since I'm someone who isn't satisfied with just slapping a bandage on an issue without fixing it at its source, I've done some digging on my end to try and provide more information on what helps reproduce the issue, as well as what the root of the cause could be.

The issue seems to mainly manifest within larger modpacks. When running any of these mods alone with FancyMenu, the bug doesn't appear. It's only when enough mods of some specific quality are installed that, after a threshold, these issues appear consistently. While I've not done enough testing to get an incredibly concrete and verbose list of every mod that adds to the issue, I've identified a list of 13 mods that, combined with FancyMenu and one of the two affected mods mentioned above, reliably recreates the issue. Those mods will be listed below in the reproduction steps. A user on the issues threads for Iris [performed their own regression and formed their own list of culprits](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/issues/2765#issuecomment-3564429683); as they said, it may be something related to the UI features all these mods add which compound into causing the bug.

While it seems unfeasible to fix an issue that only manifests when 14+ additional mods are installed, I did manage to grapple onto something a bit more concrete that could serve as a root for the issue. In both of the mods listed above, each of them, rather than using Minecraft's GameRenderer and its processBlurEffect method, recreate the logic of that function for their own uses. Tensura not only applies a custom blur strength for their own menus but also applies a toggle so that they can disable the blur during certain user actions related to HUD element rearrangement. Iris does the same thing [in their ShaderPackScreen](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/874bee3f093b0cb2218a6927ec42bb676c273122/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/gui/screen/ShaderPackScreen.java#L362) in order to create a blur that fades in and out. The key similarity between both of these mods is that they are interacting directly with the blur effect post chain, and I'm wondering if that is somehow messing up the post-processing shaders used by FancyMenu.

I've been able to lightly verify this using a bit of modding knowledge to apply mixins to each of these mods. In both cases, I reworked the code to run the vanilla renderBlurredBackground method instead of their respective custom logics. In both cases, this entirely resolved the issue. So I'm fairly certain that this is definitely the root of the issue. When mods try to change how strong the blur is, or in any way attempt to interact with the blur effect post chain, it breaks the rendering of their screens.

Having said all of this, I'm not sure whether or not there IS a fix for this on the FancyMenu side; while neither of these mods override the renderBackground logic like ModernUI does (as addressed in #971), I'm not sure where a true fix for this really lies. If this is something that can be addressed on the FancyMenu side by adjusting the post-processing blur shaders or otherwise adding in ways to work around these custom post chain adjustments, then great, that'll probably solve it for all mods that perform similar custom blur logic. But if not, if this is an issue that has to be solved on the side of the mods that are having this problem, then I'd like to hear your thoughts on how this could be resolved from their end, which I could then pass along. Any step forward on finding a more permanent fix for this issue (aside from never using menu blur ever again) will be better than letting this linger.

### How To Reproduce The Bug

1. Create a NeoForge 1.21.1 modpack with FancyMenu and the following 13 mods:
- AppleSkin
- Artifacts
- Create
- Farmer's Delight
- Iron's Spells n' Spellbooks
- Paragliders
- Relics
- Sophisticated Storage
- Supplementaries
- Tom's Simple Storage
- Twilight Forest
- Tyz's Skills
- Xaero's World Map
2. Add one or both of Tensura: Reincarnated and/or Iris Shaders to the modpack.
3. Start the game and create a new world.
4. Check the respective screens for each mod.
- For Tensura, once you have selected your race, open the main Tensura menu with B. Depending on the mods loaded, this may render correctly, or you may only see the evolution bar. If it does render correctly, you can open the settings menu using the Gear in the upper right of this screen, and the render issue should manifest more clearly there.
- For Iris Shaders, when you can access the pause menu in-world, go to Options -> Video Settings -> Shader Packs to find the Shader Pack screen. Because of the bug, it should fail to render.

issues.body:
Support thread: https://discord.com/channels/704163135787106365/1505578270932992000

Reported behavior:
When FancyMenu 3.9.1/3.9.3 is installed together with Alex's Caves 2.0.2 on Minecraft 1.20.1 Forge 47.4.15, looking at the Alex's Caves holographic projector block causes the screen to go black / flicker in that direction.

Important note:
This does not happen with FancyMenu 3.8.1, so this looks like a regression in the 3.9.x line or an interaction introduced there.

Reproduction steps:
1. Install FancyMenu 3.9.1 or 3.9.3.
2. Install Alex's Caves 2.0.2.
3. Place the holographic projector block.
4. Look at the block from the affected direction.
5. The screen goes black / flickers.

Environment:
- Minecraft 1.20.1
- Forge 47.4.15
- FancyMenu 3.9.3 (also reproducible in 3.9.1)
- Alex's Caves 2.0.2

`latest.log` does not show a crash, but it does show Alex's Caves shader warnings during startup:
```text
[Render thread/WARN]: Shader rendertype_entity_translucent_emissive could not find sampler named Sampler2 in the specified shader program.
[Render thread/WARN]: Shader alexscaves:rendertype_red_ghost could not find sampler named Sampler2 in the specified shader program.
[Render thread/WARN]: Shader bumpy could not find uniform named OutSize in the specified shader program.
```

FancyMenu startup lines from the log:
```text
[FANCYMENU] Loading v3.9.3 in client-side mode on FORGE!
[FANCYMENU] Registering resource reload listener..
[FANCYMENU] Initializing screen customization engine!
[FANCYMENU] Minecraft resource reload: STARTING
[FANCYMENU] Minecraft resource reload: FINISHED
```

The issue appears to be specific to FancyMenu 3.9.x interacting with Alex's Caves' holographic projector rendering.

issues.title: Crash when JEI sends system chat message with OPEN_FILE action while FancyMenu chat listener is active

labels.name: ⚔️ mod conflict
labels.description: A mod isn't compatible with FancyMenu

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body:
Support thread: https://discord.com/channels/704163135787106365/1505271298056523916

**Describe the bug**
When JEI's config button is clicked on a pack that does not include Configured, JEI posts a system chat message telling the user to install Configured. With FancyMenu installed, the client crashes while FancyMenu handles the system chat message listener.

The crash happens inside `OnSystemMessageReceivedInChatListener.serializeComponent`, where Minecraft throws:

```text
com.google.gson.JsonParseException: Action not allowed: OPEN_FILE
    at net.minecraft.network.chat.Component$Serializer.serialize(Component.java:164)
    at net.minecraft.network.chat.Component$Serializer.toJson(Component.java:170)
    at de.keksuccino.fancymenu.customization.listener.listeners.OnSystemMessageReceivedInChatListener.serializeComponent(OnSystemMessageReceivedInChatListener.java:45)
    at de.keksuccino.fancymenu.customization.listener.listeners.OnSystemMessageReceivedInChatListener.onSystemMessageReceivedInChat(OnSystemMessageReceivedInChatListener.java:26)
    at net.minecraft.client.multiplayer.chat.ChatListener.wrapOperation$gih000$fancymenu$wrap_addMessage_handleSystemMessage_FancyMenu(ChatListener.java:568)
    at net.minecraft.client.multiplayer.chat.ChatListener.handleSystemMessage(ChatListener.java:189)
    at net.minecraft.client.player.LocalPlayer.displayClientMessage(LocalPlayer.java:414)
    at mezz.jei.gui.overlay.ConfigButtonController.openSettings(ConfigButtonController.java:121)
```

**Reproduction**
1. Install FancyMenu + JEI, without Configured.
2. Open JEI and click the config/gear button.
3. JEI posts its missing-configurer message.
4. FancyMenu crashes while handling the system chat message.

**Environment**
- Minecraft 1.21.1
- NeoForge 21.1.228
- FancyMenu 3.9.1

issues.title: FancyMenu 3.9.1 Causes Startup Crash on Forge (Works Fine on Fabric) - Mixin Injection Failure
issues.body:
### Detailed Bug Description

When launching Minecraft 1.20.1 with Forge (tested on both 47.4.10 and 47.4.20) and FancyMenu 3.9.1 installed as the only mod in a clean environment, the game crashes during the early loading phase before reaching the main menu. The crash is caused by a Mixin injection failure in FancyMenu's Forge-specific mixin configuration file (fancymenu.forge.mixins.json).

Specifically, FancyMenu 3.9.1 attempts to inject into the Forge class net.minecraftforge.client.loading.ForgeLoadingOverlay through a method annotated as beforeRenderScreenFancyMenu. This injection is designed to hook into a method named render within ForgeLoadingOverlay, but the target method cannot be found in the tested Forge versions, resulting in an InvalidInjectionException. The full error message reads: @Inject annotation on beforeRenderScreenFancyMenu could not find any targets matching 'render' in net.minecraftforge.client.loading.ForgeLoadingOverlay. No refMap loaded.

This indicates that FancyMenu 3.9.1's Forge-specific Mixin configuration expects a method signature or internal structure in ForgeLoadingOverlay that does not exist in Forge 47.4.10 or 47.4.20. Additionally, the reference map file (fancymenu.refmap.json) fails to load for both the common and Forge mixin configurations, which may further contribute to the injection targeting failure by preventing proper obfuscation mapping resolution.

Critically, this issue is platform-specific. When tested with the same Minecraft version (1.20.1) on Fabric, FancyMenu 3.9.1 launches and functions normally without any errors. This confirms that the regression was introduced specifically in the Forge variant of FancyMenu 3.9.1, as the Fabric variant does not contain nor attempt to inject into ForgeLoadingOverlay. The Forge-exclusive class ForgeLoadingOverlay only exists in the Forge environment, so the Fabric version's code path is entirely unaffected.

The identical Forge environment works perfectly with FancyMenu 3.9.0, confirming that the regression was introduced between versions 3.9.0 and 3.9.1. Since no other mods are installed in any test scenario, mod conflicts can be ruled out entirely. The crash is fully deterministic and occurs every single time FancyMenu 3.9.1 is present in the mods folder on Forge.



### How To Reproduce The Bug

1. Install Minecraft 1.20.1 with Forge 47.4.10.
2. Create a clean mods folder with only FancyMenu 3.9.1 installed (no other mods).
3. Launch the game.
4. Observe that the game crashes during startup before reaching the main menu, with an `InvalidInjectionException` in the crash log referencing `MixinForgeLoadingOverlay`.
5. Replace FancyMenu 3.9.1 with version 3.9.0 and relaunch — the game starts normally without any issues.

issues.body:
### Description

When a scheduler set to run on launch evaluates an IF block that uses the `json` placeholder to read a JSON file in `/config/fancymenu/assets/`, the game crashes during startup.

The file I tested is valid JSON:

```json
{
  "localVersion": "7.3.0",
  "identifier": "knabbiiicraft7"
}
```

If I rename the file so the placeholder can no longer find it, the crash disappears. So the crash seems to happen when the file exists and is read by the `json` placeholder during startup scheduler evaluation.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a JSON file at `config/fancymenu/assets/simple-modpack-update-checker.json` with valid JSON content.
2. Create a schedule that runs on game start.
3. Add an IF block that compares:

```json
{"placeholder":"json","values":{"source":"/config/fancymenu/assets/simple-modpack-update-checker.json","json_path":"$.localVersion"}}
```

against:

```json
{"placeholder":"getvariable","values":{"name":"modrinth_latest"}}
```

4. Launch the game.
5. Game crashes.

If I rename the JSON file, the game starts normally.

### Expected Behavior

The `json` placeholder should read the file safely, or at least fail gracefully without crashing the game.

### Actual Behavior

The game crashes when the startup scheduler evaluates the IF block against the existing JSON file.

### Environment

- Minecraft 26.1.2
- FancyMenu 3.9.0 26.1.2

issues.title: Crash when opening top bar buttons with VulkanMod (`fancymenu_gui_smooth_rect` pipeline)

labels.name: ⚔️ mod conflict
labels.description: A mod isn't compatible with FancyMenu

labels.name: ❌ can't fix on my end
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body:
## Description
Clicking any top bar button in FancyMenu (for example: `Customization`, `Tools`) crashes the game when VulkanMod is installed.

The crash appears to happen while FancyMenu is rendering its GUI, but the failure happens inside VulkanMod while compiling the pipeline for FancyMenu's smooth rect element.

I first checked a previous log and found a malformed resource pack (`file/Harluuuu RED_v2.zip`), but after dealing with that, the crash still happens. The latest log below shows the current issue.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Install FancyMenu together with VulkanMod.
2. Launch the game.
3. Open FancyMenu's top bar.
4. Click a button like `Customization` or `Tools`.
5. The game crashes.

## Latest log
- [mclo.gs raw log](https://api.mclo.gs/1/raw/0gTYrr4)

## Support thread
- [Discord support thread](https://discord.com/channels/704163135787106365/1502936189680877598)

## Environment
- Minecraft: `26.1.2`
- Fabric Loader: `0.19.2`
- FancyMenu: `3.9.0`
- Konkrete: `1.10.1`
- Melody: `1.0.16`
- VulkanMod: `0.6.5`
- Java: `25.0.2`

## Relevant crash snippet
```text
java.lang.RuntimeException: Exception while compiling pipeline minecraft:pipeline/fancymenu_gui_smooth_rect
	at knot//net.vulkanmod.render.engine.VkGpuDevice.compilePipeline(VkGpuDevice.java:409)
	at knot//net.vulkanmod.render.engine.VkGpuDevice.compilePipeline(VkGpuDevice.java:334)
	at knot//net.vulkanmod.render.engine.VkRenderPass.setPipeline(VkRenderPass.java:87)
	at knot//com.mojang.blaze3d.systems.RenderPass.setPipeline(RenderPass.java:50)
	at knot//net.minecraft.client.gui.render.GuiRenderer.executeDraw(GuiRenderer.java:481)
	at knot//net.minecraft.client.gui.render.GuiRenderer.executeDrawRange(GuiRenderer.java:275)
	at knot//net.minecraft.client.gui.render.GuiRenderer.draw(GuiRenderer.java:255)
	at knot//net.minecraft.client.gui.render.GuiRenderer.render(GuiRenderer.java:168)
	at knot//net.minecraft.client.renderer.GameRenderer.render(GameRenderer.java:465)
```

## Notes
- This does not look like a FancyMenu-specific crash path, because the failure is inside VulkanMod's pipeline compilation.
- VulkanMod does not appear on the FancyMenu incompatibility list, so this may be a newer incompatibility.
- Temporarily removing VulkanMod makes the crash go away.

If there is any workaround on FancyMenu's side, please let me know, but right now this seems to be a VulkanMod rendering conflict with FancyMenu's GUI.

issues.title: [MC 26.1.X] Shadow line appears below custom title image element on Title Screen

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body:
**Description**
A thin dark/shadow-like line appears below a custom Image element used as the Title Screen image/logo. The line is outside the element's selection border in the editor and does not appear to come from the image file itself.

The user tested this with only FancyMenu + its dependencies installed, so this does not seem to be a mod conflict.

**Expected behavior**
An Image element should render the provided texture as-is, without adding an extra shadow line below it.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Install FancyMenu 3.9.0-26.1.1-26.1.2-fabric.
2. Create a Title Screen layout.
3. Add an Image element and use it as the title image/logo.
4. Observe a thin shadow-like line at the bottom of the image in-game.

**Environment**
- FancyMenu: 3.9.0-26.1.1-26.1.2-fabric
- Minecraft version: 26.1.2
- Fabric loader: 0.19.2
- Fabric API: 0.148.0+26.1.2
- Konkrete: 1.10.1-26.1.1-fabric
- Melody: 1.0.16-26.1.1-fabric
- Repro happens with only FancyMenu + dependencies installed

**Support thread**
https://discord.com/channels/704163135787106365/1502758982799065248

**Log**
I checked the latest log and did not see any relevant rendering exception. FancyMenu loads successfully and the log looks clean aside from an unrelated 403 profile lookup.

Relevant log snippets:
```text
[21:54:25] [Render thread/INFO]: [FANCYMENU] Loading v3.9.0 in client-side mode on FABRIC!
[21:54:25] [Render thread/INFO]: [KONKRETE] Loading v1.10.1 in client-side mode on FABRIC!
[21:54:25] [Render thread/INFO]: [MELODY] Loading v1.0.16 on FABRIC...

[21:54:29] [Render thread/INFO]: [FANCYMENU] ScreenCustomizationLayer registered: title_screen
[21:54:41] [Render thread/INFO]: [FANCYMENU] ScreenCustomizationLayer registered: title_screen
```

There is also this unrelated log entry:
```text
[21:54:25] [Download-1/WARN]: Couldn't look up profile properties for {MINECRAFT_UUID}
com.mojang.authlib.exceptions.MinecraftClientHttpException: Status: 403
```

However, if I reload FancyMenu resources, the video appears and works correctly after that.

The issue is not fully consistent: sometimes the video works normally on first load, but most of the time it does not. In the majority of cases, the background is black until I reload FancyMenu resources.

5. Observe that the background is often black on first load
6. Reload FancyMenu resources
7. Observe that the video appears and works correctly after the reload


**Expected behavior**

issues.title: Crash with customizablemenus config
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
Hey, I've been told about some crashes people are having when using your mod. After looking at the code, it seems that it doesn't handle setting the config directory to custom locations properly.

The relevant code: (this is 1.21.1 but the code is the same on other versions as well)
https://github.com/Keksuccino/FancyMenu/blob/v3-1.21.1/common/src/main/java/de/keksuccino/fancymenu/customization/ScreenCustomization.java#L66
https://github.com/Keksuccino/FancyMenu/blob/v3-1.21.1/common/src/main/java/de/keksuccino/fancymenu/customization/ScreenCustomization.java#L240-L243

2 issues there:
- The config file path is not using the fabric config directory from `FabricLoader.getConfigDir()`, it is hardcoded to `"config/"`
- If `config/fancymenu` doesn't exist, `createNewFile()` will throw an exception. A call to `getParent().mkdirs()` could be a solution to ensure the directories exist.

Edit: the same directory issue is also present here, but there's a `mkdirs()` call, so it doesn't break:
https://github.com/Keksuccino/FancyMenu/blob/v3-1.21.1-3.8.0/common/src/main/java/de/keksuccino/fancymenu/customization/customlocals/CustomLocalsHandler.java#L9

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior (e.g.):
1. Set a custom config directory for your installation, using launcher settings, or a running directory that is not `.minecraft` (and ensure you have no existing `config/fancymenu` directory)
2. Boot the game

**Expected behavior**
The mod should be respecting the fabric config directory properly and not crash if it's not possible to create it.

**Describe the bug**
FancyMenu's bad launcher detection falsely claims the entire game is a bad copy with the KubeJS startup script line "Platform.mods.fancymenu.name='put whatever name you want here';".

It did not have an issue before adding this one line to a startup script.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior (e.g.):
1. Download and install FancyMenu and KubeJS (1.21.1).
2. Make a script in startup_scripts for KubeJS.

4. Start the game
5. Everything is fine and verified in the logs
6. FancyMenu falsely flags the game and shows the popup, making it unusable.

issues.body:
**Bug Description**
In the create_world_screen I have made, every time I re-open the screen, all of my custom elements stay where I've placed them but all vanilla elements revert to their original placements.

So far and demonstrated in the video below I have found that ctrl + alt + c to toggle customization resets the screen to it's properly customized state, simply reloading Fancy Menu also works, which I then tried to link to the screen being opened in hopes of reloading to fix the screen automatically but that also hasn't worked as of yet, and the only other ways I know of to make it work properly is to go between the other two create world screen menus and back, or to disable and enable the layout.

**To Reproduce**
1. Go to the create world screen
2. Create a new layout
3. Move (seemingly) anything placed there in vanilla
4. Save the layout
5. Exit the create world screen
6. Re-open

**Expected behavior**
Once the screen is re-opened, the layout should be in the order it was placed in.

**Given Behaviour**
All vanilla elements revert to vanilla placement.

https://mclo.gs/7eiT0Gc

Setting for variables (per-variable) to set them to be "modpack-update-save" (store them outside the Minecraft instance)
issues.body:
## Describe my idea? Oh, it would be a pleasure 🫡
A way for variables to carry between instances and modpack updates would be so handy, I'm currently trying to do this with random `.txt` files in the `.minecraft` folder and it's not fun 😭

I currently have an "onboarding" system and accent colour selection that gets reset for the user after every update since the variables file is included in my exports, not including the normal `user_variables.db` in my exports is simply not an option for me either since that would remove default values that should be shipped but no need to fear because **I propose a solution:**

A toggle for existing variables to have them become "local" and referenced using another `.db` file located somewhere in `.minecraft/` (please allow a custom path like my planned `.minecraft/BUTR/`, using normal config folders there may also be issues with the official Minecraft launcher's instances being `.minecraft` too).

Having a new type of value or variable from scratch that is referenced with a different placeholder would complicate existing action scripts and variable stuff for me and probably other users, preventing a switch over. It would be easier for this variable to use the existing placeholders and have anything to do with the "local" part be exclusively in the main `user_variables.db` file and variables screen (e.g. instructions on how to find its value, its custom path for its `.db` files containing its value).

I can't think straight today lmfao so I am aware this feature request is kind of vague and messy. Even if this feature doesn't end up *exactly* how I imagined it, I would still be happy 🤣

issues.title: [1.21.11] Placeholder causes resource reload to fail

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body: _neoforge-21.11.37 fancymenu_neoforge_3.8.4 konkrete_neoforge_1.9.18 melody_neoforge_1.0.15_ --- I already wrote about this problem here. https://github.com/Keksuccino/FancyMenu/issues/1513 I spent some time figuring out the issue with my menu and found the cause of the bug. The bug is related to the use of a placeholder in the background. The placeholder is used only for testing and as an example. Whether there is a config, images from the config, or no images at all does not affect the bug — the result is always the same. **Set Background > Image > Choose Image > Open in Editir** `{"placeholder":"randomtext","values":{"source":"/config/fancymenu/assets/configs/artmenurandom.txt","interval":"5"}}` or alternatively `{"placeholder":"randomtext","values":{"path":"/config/fancymenu/assets/configs/artmenurandom.txt","interval":"60"}}` **The bug is not affected by:** - The path to the config. - Whether the config exists or not. - Whether the images specified in the config exist or not. The result is always the same. Using a placeholder in the background breaks Minecraft. **To fix the bug, you need to remove the placeholder from the background and restart Minecraft.** On previous versions of Minecraft, everything works correctly. I need this solution in order to display a random image in the background. Test files that reproduce the bug: [config_12111_fan_test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25078473/config_12111_fan_test.zip)

issues.title: [CONFIRMED] Menu background won’t apply on Singleplayer world list (1.20.1 / Forge)
issues.body:
## Description
I’m trying to set a custom menu background for the “Select World” screen (singleplayer world list) in FancyMenu v3.8.1 (Forge 47.4.10, Minecraft 1.20.1). I create a layout for that screen, enable customizations, choose a background, save the layout, and it works in the editor—but in-game the vanilla dirt background still shows up.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open the singleplayer world list and enable customization for that screen.
2. Create a new layout “for current screen.”
3. Set a custom image background and save the layout.
4. Reload the screen (or reopen the world list).

## Expected
Custom background should show instead of the dirt texture.

## Actual

issues.title: "Programmatically" spawn element instances via action
issues.body:
- Spawned element instances are not persistent and will not get saved to any files (they will stop existing when the screen/layout gets reloaded)
- The action takes an element type (via cycle button that cycles through element types) and an element body, which is simply the serialized version of an element
- When setting a type via the cycle button, the action will automatically update the default value for the body, to have a working preset for the selected type
- The body can be edited in the multiline text editor mode and has placeholder support, but there should be a way to tell the action to not simply replace all placeholders, so the user can still leave raw unparsed placeholders in the body
- When invoked, the action will add the new element instance by deserializing the body and adding the instance to the active customization layer
- Maybe it’s even possible to edit the body in the action with the actual context menu from the layout editor by having some sort of dummy layout editor instance
- The action should also let the user define an element identifier for the spawned instance (with placeholder support), to be able to communicate with the element via other actions, etc.
- There should also be a listener that triggers when an element instance got spawned via the action with custom variables `element_type` and `element_identifier` (the instance identifier), maybe also `target_screen` (where it will get injected into)

issues.title: Temporary Variables
issues.body:
- Other than normal FancyMenu variables, these variables only exist temporary and never get written to a file
- Temporary variables get reset at the end of an action script cycle
- There is an action to set a temporary variable with a unique name and value
- There is a requirement to check for the value of a temporary variable 
- There is a placeholder that gets the value of a temporary variable
- If possible, it would be good to exclude the requirement and placeholder of temporary variables from caches, so it can always get the up-to-date value (maybe add new API method to requirements and placeholders to exclude them from caching - shouldGetCached() -> default true)

issues.title: New System: Schedulers

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body:
- Schedulers have a unique ID
- Schedulers execute an action script
- Schedulers can run constantly in the background, even when no screen is open
- Schedulers can run permanently or only a certain amount of ticks
- Schedulers can run instantly or with a configurable start delay in milliseconds
- Schedulers can tick every tick or can have a configurable tick delay in milliseconds, to only tick every X milliseconds
- There is an action to start a Scheduler by its unique ID
- Schedulers can be set to get started on game launch (toggleable)
- Schedulers run on the main/render thread
- Should probably use actual Java schedulers internally and then simply execute the action script via MainThreadTaskExecutor

---

- Schedulers can be created and managed via **customization overlay menu bar -> Customization -> Manage Schedulers** (context menu entry right below "Manage Listeners")
- The ManageSchedulersScreen is built very similar to the ManageListenersScreen

issues.title: wrap_renderEntity_FancyMenu hook consuming 46% of Render Thread on Origin Realms

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
Massive render thread saturation (~46.93%) caused by the `wrap_renderEntity_FancyMenu` hook. The mod appears to be globally intercepting entity render calls even when **no entity rendering or 3D elements are used in any active layouts**. This causes significant FPS drops in areas with high densities of `item_display` entities (common on Origin Realms).

**To Reproduce**
1. Install FancyMenu 3.8.1 on Fabric 1.21.1.
2. Create layouts that contain **zero** 3D entity elements.
3. Join a server with high-poly custom models using `item_display` entities (e.g., Origin Realms).
4. Move to a high-density area like a Player Realm or the Hub.
5. Run a Spark profile and observe `fancymenu` consuming nearly 50% of the Render thread via `WorldRenderer.wrapOperation`.

**Expected behavior**
FancyMenu should only hook into entity rendering if a 3D entity element is *explicitly* used in a layout. If no such elements exist, the hook should be inactive to prevent performance loss on low-end hardware.

issues.title: Ability to separately enable/disable layouts/customizations for screens when in menu / in world
issues.body:
**Describe your idea**
A mod pack I recently downloaded to try out with friends that uses this mod to customize the main menu and to put audio on the main menu and subsequent related screens. I was noticing some inconsistencies with when the audio played from what I expected, and eventually, after trying to reproduce my self from a blank slate, boiled my findings to the following:

- Usage of a universal layout to play an audio clip
- Misconfigured mod pack settings for when screen customization is enabled (eg yes on all settings, no on multiplayer and some other related screens)
  - This is personal opinion and related to the mod, so not fully relevant here
- No way to toggle enabling of screen customization when not in a world vs when in a world.

The latter point was the biggest issue for me, given that the pack had screen customization on for `options_screen` and a lot of its children screens. This would cause the universal layout to be enabled, allowing the audio to play on these screens. However, this led to the annoying side effects where the menu music would play anytime you hit escape to "pause" the game.

I looked though the available options to see if there was a way to turn off the customization or layout when a world was loaded, but I couldnt find one. Adding something like that would be quite helpful for mod users / pack makers.

An alternative route that could help this problem would be to add a setting to ui elements that lets them get loaded on a given screen and stay loaded until there is a change in world state. Basically, on title screen load, create audio element A, which does not get deleted until the game is closed or a world is created / joined.

issues.title: Settings screen widgets not customizable in MC 1.21.11
"PiP Window" System

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body:
This is a new system that will be used for FancyMenu's UIs first. 

- Should get created in the `de.keksuccino.fancymenu.util.rendering.ui.pipwindow` package.
- The system should use `GuiGraphics` by default for most of its rendering-related logic.
- It creates an operating-system-like window inside the Minecraft game that has a normal title bar with window title, icon, maximize/un-maximize and close buttons.
- The window has a window body that can be filled with content and should implement `Renderable` for that.
- The window has a window border around body and title bar.
- The window should be movable/draggable by grabbing the title bar.
- The window should be resizable when hovering over the edges and corners.
- The window should implement `ContainerEventHandler` for listening to GUI events and for registering child GUI elements.
- There should be a full handler for handling currently open windows. Multiple can be open at the same time.
- Windows should be aware of their parent and child windows.
- Windows should have a way to get their input locked when a child window is open, so we don't need to close the parent when we want a child to finish its work first before input is allowed again for the parent window.
- Windows should hold a normal `Screen` instance. This screen instance gets rendered as body.
  - The screen instance's GUI event listeners should get routed through the Window, so the screen can be interacted with. 
  - The screen instance needs to get resized with the window and should always have the current window size as screen size (width + height).
  - The screen probably needs to get translated to the correct position of the window via `GuiGraphics`.
  - All mouse positions need to get corrected for the screen, so the screen receives the correct actual mouse positions instead of messed up ones because of position translate.
  - Setting a new screen instance for the window should call Screen#init() of the new instance.
  - Screen instances of windows do NOT get set as Minecraft.screen instance!

issues.title: New System: Functions
issues.body:
Functions are basically just action scripts, one script per function.

They exist for two main purposes:

- Via an action it is possible to execute functions by ID.
- Via a placeholder it is possible to execute a function by ID that returns a string value.
  - This is a special case where a function is not always a VOID, but can also be a GET STRING basically.
  - Need to figure out a way to implement this new special case in the existing action script system, maybe with a special action that only works inside functions that sets the return value.

Functions get managed in **menu bar -> Customization -> Manage Functions**, at the same spot where the entry to manage listeners is placed.

Each function has a unique ID (defined by the user, like for variables).

The "Manage Functions" screen should look and work similar to the screen to manage listeners.

issues.title: "Play Audio" action

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body:
- Plays an audio, just like the `AudioElement`, but independent of elements
- Just like the `AudioElement`, the action uses FancyMenu's audio resource system (ResourceSupplier, AudioResource, etc.)
- Since it's possible the audio resource is not ready when the action gets executed, we should start a thread that waits for the audio to be ready (with 10 sec timeout) and plays it in the main thread (MainThreadTaskExecutor - PRE TICK) once it's ready
- Once the audio started, it will play to the end (it can't get stopped)
- Has options to set the sound channel and the base volume of the audio
- Has an option to specify the audio file path (check `ShowToastAction` for how to make a good file chooser in an action)

issues.body:
## Problem:
It is **impossible** to remove or disable a mod with FancyMenu _(even with the "On Quit Minecraft" listener)_ because the mods .jar is open in Minecraft unless you run an OS-specific or Python script when you close the game. This means that having FancyMenu manage your mods is not a viable solution and in my menus I can't have users remove the mods they add.

## Possible solution:
Run some kind of *(maybe external)* Java to delete, move or rename a mods .jar file AFTER the game closes somehow OR set some kind of silly Fabric/Neoforge argument to just not load the mod on next launch and THEN mess with the mod. With this code happening after the game closes it shouldn't have a problem deleting the file but it's just _how_ do you get external Java stuff running and _will people like it?_

issues.title: New Customization Type: Global Customizations

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body:
A special type of customizations that happen outside of layouts and affect the whole client instead of just specific menus that have customizations enabled.

- They are smaller, mostly save-to-apply customizations (or "tweaks") that do not need menus to have customizations enabled.
- The "existing Custom Window Icon" and "Custom Window Title" would then fall under this new category.
- Global customizations can be accessed via **menu bar -> Customization -> Global Customizations**, in the same menu bar as the "Manage Listeners" option.
- Global Customizations get applied to every menu in the game (and other non-menu parts), even if menus do not have customizations enabled.
- Global customizations should not use the layout system and instead apply their customizations in a more hardcoded way via Mixin injections (basically replacing the normal Vanilla logic with the customized one, if customizations are set)
- Global customization settings should make use of the existing text input and file/resource chooser implementations, just like other parts of the mod.
- Global customization settings should get saved in the mod's options (`FancyMenu.getOptions()`).
- Global customizations should use FancyMenu's resource system for handling resources like images and audio, just like other parts of the mod.

Global customization options:

- [x] Custom Window Icon
- [x] Custom Window Title
- [x] Custom Button Background Textures (Normal, Hover, Inactive)
- [x] Custom Slider Background Texture
- [x] Custom Slider Handle Textures (Normal, Hover, Imactive)
- [x] Custom Background Panorama (background of all screens; should use FancyMenu's existing panorama system for replacing the default panorama with a custom one loaded by the user)
- [x] Custom Menu Music Tracks (should work like Vanilla menu music and randomly pick a track from the tracks list)
- [x] Custom Button Click Sound (inject in `playDownSound()`)
- [x] Custom Menu Background Texture (for older MC versions) (should be a tile texture that connects seamlessly, just like the original dirt texture)

issues.title: "File Got Selected" listener

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body:
This listener triggers when a file got selected via the "Select File" action. It triggers both when the selection got cancelled and when a file got selected.

If a file got selected, the listener needs to trigger AFTER the action finished copying the file to the new directory.

The action has support for copying files to the Minecraft instance directory AND `.minecraft`, which does not have to be the actual instance directory. Make sure to check the action to see how it handles/resolves paths.

The listener provides the following custom variables:

- `absolute_source_file_path` = The absolute path of the original location of the selected file. This is empty when no file got selected or the selection failed in another way.
- `resource_path` = Returns the short path of the new location the file got copied to (like `/config/fancymenu/assets/image.png` when in the actual MC instance or something like `.minecraft/config/....`, with the `.minecraft/` prefix, when copied to the `.minecraft` directory. This is empty when no file got selected or the selection failed in another way.
- `success` = If the selection was a success or got cancelled or otherwise interrupted (by an error or whatever) (true/false).

issues.title: "Select File" action

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev

issues.body: ## **My actually really cool idea** Just like when you want to open/select a file in a program and it opens this "Open/Select File" window of File Explorer where it lets you browse and select the file you want to open. This action would open the same OS-specific Open/Select File popup as extra window, and would talk back to Minecraft/FancyMenu when a file got selected or the selection got cancelled. The action should have a setting to customize the file type that the Open/Select File window is looking for - The box with the label: `All Files (*.*)`. With that capability I could have it only look for `.png` files if I'm doing something like a wallpaper. ## How would this work? You should be able to specify in the action where the selected file is copied to (inside the MC instance directory AND .minecraft, exact same logic as all other file-related actions). The target path would include the file name, just like the Copy File action. It is important that the Open/Select File popup has full access to the whole OS and is not sandboxed like the target path, because the user has to select the file, so it can't be abused by automating it. The popup should be cross-OS compatible (showing native Windows select popup on Window, native macOS one on macOS, etc. -- LWJGL maybe has a helper for that). Next, I'm gonna explain how this would work when used. So, lets say that within this Open/Select File popup I select an image called "keksuccino.jpeg" from "C:\Users\User\Downloads" and I have this file set to be copied to the new file path of: `/config/fancymenu/assets/background.jpeg`. Now when I use the image `/config/fancymenu/assets/background.jpeg` it should be the same image as I'd previously uploaded ("keksuccino.jpeg").

## **Definitions**
When one is listening to Spotify, YouTube or an MP3 and they can see the album cover and song/video name in some places outside of the platform they are viewing it on then I will call this the "Currently Playing Media" though there is probably a better name for this.

## **The placeholders**

Currently Playing Media Name/Text - If I am for some reason watching [the element animator tutorial by Keks](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F9S8cIPssww&t=574s) then this placeholder should return `FancyMenu | How to Use the Element Animator`

issues.title: UPDATE LOCALIZATIONS !!
Update documentation for Scoreboard Score placeholder (explanation inside)
issues.body:
The Scoreboard Score placeholder can only return a value if the selected objective is displayed in some slot (i.e. sidebar, below_name, list, or sidebar.team.<colour>), presumably because that's necessary for the objective's scores to be sent to the client and for FM to have access to them.

It'd be helpful if this requirement could be stated in the documentation for that placeholder to e.g. save someone spending a week on and off trying to get it to work, nearly giving up thinking it was broken somehow, and then discovering what was going on purely by accident 😂

e.g.:

## Scoreboard Score (scoreboard_score)

Returns the score value of a player for a specific objective.

`{"placeholder":"scoreboard_score","values":{"player":"Steve","objective":"kills"}}`

Example output: `42`

**Important:** The chosen objective must be displayed in order for FM to be able to access the scores, by running e.g. `/scoreboard objectives setdisplay sidebar <objective_name>` The objective can be displayed in any slot i.e. `sidebar`, `below_name`, `list`, or `sidebar.team.<colour>`.

It feels very random, but FM seems to break scrolling in the SkillZ GUI screen. issues.title: NBT Data placeholder always returns nothing

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body:
([latest.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22260903/latest.zip) because the bug report asked for it, though I'm 99.9% sure there's nothing useful in there. I had to zip it because, unzipped, it's >50mb somehow)

**Describe the bug**

Using the NBT Data placeholder appears to always return nothing. I have tested:

- Armor stand
- Marker entity
- Chicken
- Myself

I've tested with a variety of keys including `Tags`, `Pos[0]`, `foodLevel` (the default one in the example Placeholder).

I'm certain that the selectors I used are correct.

The 'explain like I'm 5 years old' you asked for (sorry if this isn't what you meant):

Every entity in Minecraft (mobs, items, players, etc.) is stored as a big block of NBT data.
Think of it as a tree. Inside it are 'keys'; each key stores something about the entity — its position, health, name, tags, etc. The keys have specific names e.g. `Health`, `Tags`, `Pos`, `Rotation` etc. Keys can hold numbers, text, list, more nested objects etc. You can use `/data get` to read the whole blob, or specific keys

---

**Getting the entity’s whole NBT**

Summon a chicken named `test`:

```mcfunction
/summon minecraft:chicken ~ ~ ~ {CustomName:'"test"'}
```

Then get the chicken's NBT:

```mcfunction
/data get entity @e[type=minecraft:chicken,limit=1,sort=nearest,name=test]
```

Example output:

```
[Entity data: {
  id: "minecraft:chicken",
  CustomName: "\"test\"",
  Health: 4.0f,
  Pos: [123.0d, 64.0d, -45.0d],
  Motion: [0.0d, 0.0d, 0.0d],
  UUID: [I; 123456, 789012, 345678, 901234],
  ...other keys...
}]
```

---

**Getting a specific key from the NBT**

The `Pos` key stores the entity’s position as an array: `[x, y, z]`. To get just the X coordinate:

```mcfunction
/data get entity @e[type=minecraft:chicken,limit=1,sort=nearest,name=test] Pos[0]
```

Example output:

```
123.0d
```

---


**To Reproduce**

1. Summon a chicken with the CustomName test (or rename one 'test' with a nametag)
2. Create an FM text box with the placeholder `{"placeholder":"nbt_data_get","values":{"source_type":"entity","entity_selector":"@e[type=minecraft:chicken,name=text,limit=1]","nbt_path":"Health","return_type":"value"}}` as its text content
3. Create an FM button with the action send chat message, with the same placeholder as #3.
4. Enter GUI - text box is blank. Press button - a blank chat message is sent.

**Expected behavior**
Text box contains `4f` and chat message says `4f`

**Game Log**
Please always include your `.minecraft/logs/latest.log` file **right after the issue happened**.
Please don't send the whole log as plain text here. Upload the file to https://gist.github.com and send the link.
DON'T SEND LOG SNIPPETS OR CRASH LOGS, PLEASE SEND THE WHOLE LATEST.LOG FILE!

**Screenshots**
If screenshots would help to explain the issue, please include these.

**Basic Information (please complete the following information):**

 - FancyMenu 3.6.4
 - Fabric 0.16.10
 - Minecraft 1.21.1

issues.title: NBT Data Placeholder (nbt_data_get) - Enchanted Items Missing from Inventory NBT

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body:
Discord Thread Link: https://discord.com/channels/704163135787106365/1411698937806721035

**Minecraft Version:** 1.21.8
**Mod Loader:** Fabric 0.132.0
**FancyMenu Version:** 3.7.0
**SpiffyHUD Version:** 3.0.2

**Description:**
When using the nbt_data_get placeholder to retrieve player inventory data (specifically, the Inventory NBT tag), enchanted items are consistently missing from the returned NBT list. This behavior is observed in both singleplayer and multiplayer environments.

**Steps to Reproduce:**
1.  Launch Minecraft 1.21.8 with Fabric (0.132.0), FancyMenu (3.7.0), and SpiffyHUD (3.0.2).
2.  In-game, acquire any enchanted item (e.g., an enchanted diamond sword or pickaxe).
3.  Place this enchanted item into your inventory or hotbar.
4.  Open the FancyMenu/SpiffyHUD editor.
5.  Create a text element or similar display to show the full player inventory NBT using the nbt_data_get placeholder with nbt_path="Inventory" and a return_type of "snbt" or "json".
    *   Example: {"placeholder":"nbt_data_get","values":{"source_type":"entity","entity_selector":"@s","nbt_path":"Inventory","return_type":"snbt"}}
6.  Observe the output: The Inventory list returned by nbt_data_get` will conspicuously omit the enchanted item, while other non-enchanted items will be present.
Expected Behavior:
The nbt_data_get placeholder, when querying the Inventory NBT tag, should return all items present in the player's inventory, including enchanted items, regardless of whether it's singleplayer or multiplayer.

Actual Behavior:
Enchanted items are not included in the Inventory list returned by nbt_data_get.

Additional Context:
The in-game "NBT Player Helper" object (accessed through FancyMenu's tools) does correctly list and recognize the enchanted items and their NBT data, indicating that the information is generally accessible to the mod.
This issue occurs consistently in both singleplayer and multiplayer.
It specifically affects enchanted items; non-enchanted items (including tools without enchantments) are retrieved correctly.

This suggests that the nbt_data_get placeholder (or its underlying NBT/JsonPath parsing logic) has a problem processing or including enchanted item NBT data.

issues.title: New System: LISTENERS

labels.name: ✅ implemented/fixed in dev
labels.description: Label for maintainers. Do not set on your own!

issues.body:
## Basic Functionality

- Listeners constantly listen to specific events
- Listeners work on a global level, they work outside layouts and even menus, constantly listening, even if no menu is open (in a world/server)
- Listeners execute an action script when triggered
- Listeners can "send" data to their actions (and condition requirements) by using the existing systems for custom variables in requirements/actions (currently only used for sliders and checkboxes)
- Listeners have NO SETTINGS (everything important gets sent as custom vars and the action script should handle the logic part)
- Uses a similar registry flow as placeholders/requirements/actions, which means addons can easily add new listeners
- The system could be used as base for an addon in the future that plays cinematics in-world

## Listeners

- [x] On Variable Value Updated
  - Triggers when a variable value gets set/updated
  - Sends `variable_name`, `old_variable_value` and `new_variable_value` as custom vars
- [x] On Mouse Moved
  - Triggers when the user moves the mouse cursor
  - Gets triggered constantly as long as the mouse keeps moving
  - Sends `mouse pos x`, `mouse pos y`, `mouse move delta x` and `mouse move delta y` as custom vars
- [x] On Mouse Scrolled
  - Triggers when the user scrolls with the mouse
  - Gets triggered constantly as long as the user keeps scrolling the mouse
  - Sends `scroll delta y` as custom var
- [x] On Keyboard Key Pressed
  - Triggers when the user presses a keyboard key
  - Should trigger continuously like in Vanilla as long as the key is pressed 
  - Sends `key_name`, `key_keycode`, `key_scancode`, `key_modifiers` as custom var
- [x] On Keyboard Key Released
  - Triggers when the user stops pressing a keyboard key
  - Sends `key_name`, `key_keycode`, `key_scancode`, `key_modifiers` as custom var
- [x] On Char Typed
  - Triggers when the user types a char
  - Sends `char` as custom var
- [x] On Mouse Button Clicked
  - Triggers when the user starts pressing a mouse button
  - Should trigger ONCE per click (not continuously as long as the button is down)
  - Sends `button` (`left`, `right`), `mouse_pos_x`, `mouse_pos_y` as custom vars
- [x] On Mouse Button Released
  - Triggers when the user stops pressing a mouse button
  - Sends `button` (`left`, `right`), `mouse_pos_x`, `mouse_pos_y` as custom vars
- [x] On Chat Message Received
  - Gets triggered when the client receives a chat message
  - Sends `chat_message_string` (unformatted message string), `chat_message_component` (serialized component json), `sender_uuid`, `sender_name` as custom vars
- [x] On Chat Message Sent
  - Gets triggered when the client sends a chat message
  - Sends `chat_message_string` (unformatted message string), `chat_message_component` (serialized component json) as custom vars
- [x] On Open Screen
  - Triggers when opening a menu, right after the new menu got opened in `setScreen()`, so actions can override it ("Open Screen or Custom GUI" action)
  - Sends `screen_identifier` as custom var
- [x] On Close Screen
  - Triggers when closing a menu, right after the old menu got closed in `setScreen()`
  - Sends the `screen_identifier` as custom var
- [x] On Server Joined
  - Triggers when the client finished connecting to a server (when successfully connected to server)
  - Sends `server_IP` as custom var
- [x] On Server Left
  - Triggers when the client disconnects from a server
  - Sends `server_IP` as custom var
- [x] On Other Player Joined World/Server
  - Triggers when a user joins the current world/server
  - Sends `player_name` and `player_uuid` as custom vars
- [x] On Other Player Left World/Server
  - Triggers when a user left the current world/server
  - Sends `player_name` and `player_uuid` as custom vars
- [x] On Quit Minecraft
  - Tries to trigger right before the client gets closed (not sure if I can implement this in a stable way, since shutdown hooks do not always work)
- [x] On Death
  - Triggers when the player dies, right after the Death Screen got opened via `setScreen()`, so actions can override it ("Open Screen or Custom GUI" action)
  - Sends `days_survived`, `death_reason`, `death_pos_x`, `death_pos_y`, `death_pos_z` as custom vars
- [x] On Other Player Died
  - Triggers when a player dies in the current world/server
  - Sends `player_name`, `player_uuid`, `death_pos_x`, `death_pos_y`, `death_pos_z` as custom vars
- [x] On Enter Biome
  - Triggers when the player enters a biome
  - Sends `biome key` as custom var
- [x] On Leave Biome
  - Triggers when the player leaves a biome
  - Sends `biome key` as custom var
- [x] On Enter Structure
  - Triggers when the player enters a structure (village, ship wreck, etc.)
  - Sends `structure key` as custom var
- [x] On Leave Structure
  - Triggers when the player leaves a structure (village, ship wreck, etc.)
  - Sends `structure key` as custom var
- [x] On Start Swimming
  - Triggers when the player starts swimming
  - Sends `fluid type` as custom var
- [x] On Stop Swimming
  - Triggers when the player stops swimming
  - Sends `fluid type` as custom var

  - Triggers ONCE when stepping on the block
  - Sends `block_key`, `block_pos_x`, `block_pos_y`, `block_pos_z` as custom vars
- [x] On Looking At Block
  - Triggers when the player looks at a block (when the crosshair is aiming at it)
  - Triggers ONCE when looking at the block
  - Sends `block key` and `distance_to_player` as custom vars
- [x] On Looking At Entity
  - Triggers when the player looks at an entity (when the crosshair is aiming at it)
  - Triggers only ONCE when the player starts looking at it (and again if the player looked away and then looked at it again)
  - Sends `entity_key`, `distance_to_player`, `entity_pos_x`, `entity_pos_y`, `entity_pos_z`, `entity_uuid` as custom vars
- [x] On Entity In Sight
  - Triggers when the player can see an entity (when the entity is in view / inside the FOV)
  - Triggers only ONCE when the entity starts being in view (and again if it got out view and then came back in view)
  - Sends `entity_key`, `distance_to_player`, `entity_pos_x`, `entity_pos_y`, `entity_pos_z`, `entity_uuid` as custom vars
- [x] On Interacted With Entity
  - Triggers when the player interacts with an entity (should be only right-clicking in most cases?)
  - Sends `entity_key`, `entity_pos_x`, `entity_pos_y`, `entity_pos_z`, `entity_uuid` as custom vars

  - Sends `entity_key`, `entity_pos_x`, `entity_pos_y`, `entity_pos_z`, `entity_uuid` as custom vars
- [x] On Entity Unmounted
  - Triggers when the player stops riding an entity
  - Sends `entity_key`, `entity_pos_x`, `entity_pos_y`, `entity_pos_z`, `entity_uuid` as custom vars
